A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 10-page versions of the same GDNet study, with corresponding methods, equations, datasets, and figures. All pages were inspected; both end with references, and neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 and Tables 1–3 report original GDNet benchmark results and component/loss ablations on AIM 2024 and Compressed-NYU.

after.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 and Tables 1–4 retain original GDNet results and add internal-component ablations and attention-count experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the FGDE/DCPM attention operations, GGE/LFR reconstruction using QR decomposition and a Neumann-series approximation, depth decoder, and SILog objective. The new experiments test existing components without establishing a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the TartanAir-derived AIM 2024 dataset and synthesized Compressed-NYU for depth recovery under combined downsampling, bit-depth compression, and noise. No dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially expands its learned-method comparisons by adding UniDepth V1, UniDepth V2, iDisc, and AdaBins alongside the retained Depth Anything variants and SGNet. Bicubic and bilinear are removed from this comparison. The AIM comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds experimental controls without DCPM or LFR and tests SA/CA counts of (2,1), (3,1), (1,2), and (1,3) against (1,1). Existing dataset splits, augmentation, 400-epoch training, batch size 2, learning-rate schedule, and MAE/RMSE evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 ablates whole FGDE/GGE encoders and the loss function. v3 additionally isolates DCPM and LFR in Table 3 and introduces attention-count sensitivity analysis in Table 4. This substantially extends the analysis to the specific internal components and attention depth.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added experiments retain point-estimate MAE/RMSE reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 systematically reverse the retained Compressed-NYU MAE/RMSE assignments: GDNet changes from 0.0739/0.0322 to 0.0322/0.0739. v3 also adds baseline, component-ablation, and attention-count results and removes interpolation results from Table 2. Table 1 remains unchanged. These are reporting revisions and expanded evidence, not demonstrated improvements to the same model. v3 Section 4.2 additionally gives RMSE as 0.739, contradicting Table 2's 0.0739.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18, including the least-squares reconstruction, QR-based projection derivation, and SILog formulation, are retained. No mathematical definition, formal assumption, proof, or derivation is substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about decoupling detailed and global geometry, FGDE/GGE contributions, superior reconstruction, and the AIM challenge win. The additional experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting FGDE to detail preservation, GGE to noise suppression, and SILog to reconstruction quality remain substantively unchanged. The attention-count paragraph reports selecting the best configuration without adding a mechanism explanation or substantive limitation.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the promise that code will become available into a statement of availability with a concrete GitHub address. Existing hardware, optimizer, augmentation, and training disclosures are retained; the PDFs alone do not verify repository contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for AdaBins, iDisc, UniDepth, degradation-oriented blind depth super-resolution, and incomplete-data correlations, while removing v1 references 26, 31, 34, and 51. Section 2's related-work organization and the paper's novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited wording, terminology, and caption edits, removal of the affiliation line, and addition of funding acknowledgments. The section sequence and most explanatory paragraphs remain intact; pagination changes do not represent substantive reorganization.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 4, expands Table 3 with DCPM/LFR columns and rows, and moves Table 2 beside Table 1 on page 7. Figures retain their substantive visual content, with revised captions, labels, sizing, and spacing. The overall two-column presentation remains similar.

improvement.justification: v3 provides better evidence for architectural choices through targeted DCPM/LFR ablations and attention-count experiments, broadens benchmark comparisons, and supplies code access information. It also resolves the apparent tabular MAE/RMSE transposition. These gains are limited by sparse discussion of the new analyses and the new Section 4.2 RMSE inconsistency, 0.739 versus Table 2's 0.0739. Overall, the evidence and documentation improve without fundamentally changing the study.
